title: Tomato leaf spot management
text: Early blight and septoria leaf spot cause dark spots on tomato leaves. Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation before rain, and use copper-based fungicide if disease pressure is high. Treatment cost is typically moderate; delay sprays if heavy rain is forecast within 24 hours.

title: Tomato fertilizer rules
text: Tomato needs balanced NPK. Excess nitrogen increases foliage and disease risk. Prefer split fertilizer doses. With limited budget, prioritize potassium and calcium during fruiting over additional nitrogen.

title: Tomato selling and storage
text: Tomato is perishable with short shelf life. If mandi prices are falling and storage or cold chain is unavailable, consider staged early harvest of ripe fruit rather than holding for a recovery that may not come.

title: Potato late blight
text: Late blight thrives in cool wet weather. Scout lower leaves, destroy infected haulms, and apply approved fungicide preventively when rain is expected. Do not spray immediately before heavy rainfall.

title: Potato soil and NPK
text: Potato prefers well-drained loamy soil. Maintain adequate potassium for tuber quality. Avoid waterlogging which raises disease and reduces marketable yield.

title: Maize nutrient deficiency
text: Yellowing of lower leaves often indicates nitrogen deficiency. Apply urea in splits. Confirm soil moisture before top dressing. Maize responds poorly to drought at tasseling.

title: Maize fall armyworm basics
text: Scout whorls for larvae. Early detection allows mechanical control or targeted insecticide. Avoid blanket sprays when beneficial insects are active.

title: Irrigation and rain timing
text: Skip irrigation when significant rainfall is forecast. Standing water increases fungal disease risk for tomato and potato. Schedule sprays after rain when leaves dry.

title: Limited budget decision rule
text: Under tight budget, compare treatment cost against expected salvageable yield and current mandi price. If expected post-treatment profit is negative and prices are falling, selling early or reducing input intensity may be safer than full treatment.

title: Sprayer equipment guidance
text: For small farms under 3 acres, knapsack or rental battery sprayers are usually more cost-effective than owning tractor-mounted sprayers. Factor rental into treatment cost.
